title: Tenant Stability Predictive Signals Runbook
author: Aisha Patel
body:
Purpose and scope
-----------------
This runbook defines the predictive signals, automated enrichment, and operational play for preventing tenant instability during the first 90 days after provisioning and at scale. It is intended for Customer Success Engineers (CSEs), SREs, Platform Engineers, and on-call Support. The playbook covers detection thresholds, triage steps, automated mitigations, customer communications, and post-incident follow-up templates.

Why this exists
-----------------
- Many early-stage incidents for enterprise tenants are preceded by measurable leading indicators (cache miss spikes, request token variance, route fan-out changes, model mismatch regressions).
- Acting on signals reduces severity, shortens time to mitigation, and reduces churn risk.
- Provides clear ownership and automation recipes to reduce manual toil.

Key definitions and roles
------------------------
- Tenant: A single enterprise customer tenant (dedicated or hosted).
- Predictive signal: A metric or composite metric that historically correlates with a stability degradation within 1–72 hours.
- Owner roles:
  - CSE (Customer Success Engineer): Primary customer-facing technical owner during onboarding and early life.
  - SRE: Operational owner responsible for infra/slo remediation and incident escalation.
  - Platform Eng: Owner for deployment/rollback actions and model routing policies.
  - Escalation Lead: Designated cross-functional lead for Sev2+ events.

SLOs referenced
---------------
- Tenant 99p tail latency (in-region): 500 ms target, 750 ms warning, 1200 ms Sev2 threshold
- 95p success rate (per-tenant, per-hour): 99.5% target, 99.0% warning, 97.0% Sev2 threshold
- KV cache hit rate (per-tenant, rolling 10m): 85% target, 70% warning, 50% Sev2 threshold

Priority predictive signals (ranked)
----------------------------------
1) KV cache miss rate sudden increase (delta > 20 pp within 10 minutes)
   - Why: Causes token re-computation and tail latency spikes.
   - Detection: rolling10m_kv_cache_miss_rate{tenant_id="$TENANT"} - alert if > 0.20 AND increase > 0.20 vs prev10m
   - PromQL example: (increase(kv_cache_misses_total{tenant="$TENANT"}[10m]) / increase(kv_cache_requests_total{tenant="$TENANT"}[10m])) > 0.2
2) Token-per-request (TPR) variance spike (p99 TPR > baseline * 1.6)
   - Why: Unexpected prompt/agent behavior or malformed client input causes cost and latency escalation.
   - Detection: compare p99(TPR, 30m) vs tenant baseline over 7d.
3) Model-variant mismatch errors (client requested variant not available + auto-fallback rate > 5%)
   - Why: Rollouts or capacity limits can trigger silent fallbacks and degrade quality.
4) Request fan-out increase (downstream retries causing multiple backend requests)
   - Why: Retries/backpressure loops amplify load; common during intermittent network issues.
5) 99p latency climb above warning threshold while success rate holds steady
   - Why: Often first sign of degraded hardware or contention (GPU saturation, NVMe throttling).

Alerting taxonomy and severity mapping
------------------------------------
- Predictive Warning: Single-signal threshold crossed (pager suppressed, Slack #cs-early-warning posted, ticket created).
- Predictive Sev3: Two related signals active for > 15m; page CSE and SRE (Slack @oncall and create incident record).
- Predictive Sev2: Any Sev2 SLO breached OR composite signal score > 0.8 for 30m. Pager escalation: SRE, Platform Eng, Escalation Lead.

Automated enrichment and alert payload content
--------------------------------------------
Every predictive alert must include:
- tenant_id, tenant_name, customer_tier (dedicated/hosted/private), region, active_model, model_variant, recent_deployments (IDs), recent_rollout_percentages, last_2h_kv_cache_rates, last_2h_tpr_p95_p99, last_5m_error_types, related_traces (URLs), recent_autoscale_events, current_capacity_pool_id
- Attach: 1) top 10 slow traces (sampled), 2) snapshot of the last successful and failed request payloads (redact PII), 3) CSV of per-route qps last 60m.

Initial automated remediation recipes (safe by default)
----------------------------------------------------
These automation recipes are executed by the Platform Eng runbook bot (redwood-ops). All actions are reversible.
1) Read-only route throttle (rate-limit non-critical routes)
   - Command: redwood-ops route throttle --tenant $TENANT --route-pattern "/api/v1/agents/*" --qps 10 --reason "auto-kvcache-miss-mitigation"
2) Increase KV cache warming priority for tenant (pin prefixes to warm pool)
   - Command: redwood-ops cache prioritize --tenant $TENANT --prefix-list-file recent-prefixes.csv
3) Temporary model routing to stable variant (no config changes to customer code)
   - Command: redwood-ops reroute --tenant $TENANT --from-variant v2 --to-variant v1 --duration 30m --annot "predictive-signal-failback"
4) Allocate burst capacity from dedicated reserve (if tenant is on Dedicated plan)
   - Command: redwood-ops capacity allocate --pool reserve-dedicated --tenant $TENANT --minutes 60

Triage play (ordered steps)
---------------------------
1) Receive alert and review automated enrichment (within 5m).
   - Who: CSE + oncall SRE (piggyback on Slack alert).
2) Validate signal: check KV cache hit/miss graphs, top traces, and recent deploy IDs.
   - Who: SRE.
3) If KV cache miss delta is confirmed, trigger cache prioritize recipe (automated or manual).
   - Who: Platform Eng or redwood-ops bot.
4) If TPR spike present, open Customer Insights ticket and ask CSM to validate recent prompt changes or agents.
   - Who: CSE + CSM.
5) If model-variant fallback is >5% or quality regression signalled, initiate controlled rollback to last known-good model variant and notify customer (see Customer Communication templates).
   - Who: Platform Eng + CSE.
6) If latency continues to degrade or success rate drops below 97%, escalate to Sev2 and follow incident process (page Execs per escalation matrix).

Customer communications (templates)
--------------------------------
Use these templates to reduce confusion and set expectations. Customize cadence depending on severity.
- Early-warning (Predictive Warning, not service impacting):
  Subject: Redwood – Early Notice: Observed increased request variance for your tenant
  Body: Hello <Customer Contact>, our monitoring has detected an increase in request complexity for tenant <tenant_name> that may cause degraded latency. We are applying targeted, reversible mitigations (cache warming and route throttles) and will update in 30 minutes. No action is required from your side unless you observed recent agent/prompt changes.
- Action required (Sev3):
  Subject: Redwood – Attention: Elevated errors affecting some requests
  Body: Hello <Customer Contact>, we are investigating elevated errors and have initiated mitigations. Please confirm whether you have recently modified prompts, added agents, or changed request fan-out. We will provide a status update within 20 minutes.
- Outage/Sev2:
  Subject: Redwood – Incident: Impacting availability for <tenant_name>
  Body: Hello <Customer Contact>, we are actively responding to an incident impacting request success for your tenant. Our teams (SRE, Platform, CSE) are engaged. We will provide ETA for restoration and next steps within 15 minutes. We will also give a post-incident summary after remediation.

Escalation matrix and contact list
----------------------------------
- Sev3: CSE -> SRE on-call -> Platform Eng (pager)
- Sev2: CSE -> SRE on-call -> Platform Eng -> Escalation Lead -> Head of Customer Success (page all)
- Pager channels: Ops PagerDuty, #cs-early-warning, #prod-incidents
- Contact list (on-call rota referenced from roster page):
  - CSE: oncall-cse@redwood.ai
  - SRE oncall: ops-oncall@redwood.ai
  - Platform Eng: platform-oncall@redwood.ai

Post-incident follow-up checklist
--------------------------------
- Short-term (within 24h):
  1) Confirm root cause hypothesis and mitigation timeline.
  2) Share initial incident summary with customer and internal stakeholders.
  3) Create postmortem ticket and assign owners.
- Long-term (within 14 days):
  1) Implement durable fixes (hotfix or config change).
  2) Add predictive signal tuning (threshold/weight) to the sentinel rules if noisy or missed.
  3) Schedule QBR discussion if customer impact > 2 days or repeat issues occurred within 90 days.

Runbook maintenance and signal governance
----------------------------------------
- Quarterly signal review: CS + SRE + Platform will review predictive signal performance (precision, recall, false positives).
- Owners must adjust thresholds and enrichment payload fields if root cause patterns change.
- New signals should be documented with: name, owner, detection query, historical precision/recall, and a test harness for simulation.

Telemetry and dashboards (reference)
-----------------------------------
- Dashboards: Tenant Stability Overview (per-tenant filter), KV Cache Heatmap, Model Variant Rollout Monitor, Route Fanout Explorer.
- Key Grafana panels and queries required for triage are linked from the alert (always include dashboard URL in the alert).
- Required metrics: kv_cache_misses_total, kv_cache_requests_total, request_tokens_per_request, request_latency_p50_p95_p99, request_success_count, model_variant_fallback_count, autoscale_events_total

Playbook automation safety and governance
----------------------------------------
- Auto-mitigations are enabled for enterprise tenants after a 7-day probation window and only if the customer has opted into "proactive mitigations" during onboarding.
- All automated actions are logged and must include: actor, reason, diff of the config change, and rollback command.
- For restricted tenants (high-security), auto actions are dry-run only and require manual approval by the customer contact.

Appendix A — PromQL examples and helper queries
------------------------------------------------
- KV cache miss rate (10m):
  increase(kv_cache_misses_total{tenant="$TENANT"}[10m]) / increase(kv_cache_requests_total{tenant="$TENANT"}[10m])
- p99 tokens per request (30m):
  histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(tokens_per_request_bucket{tenant="$TENANT"}[30m])) by (le))
- Composite predictive score (example heuristic):
  0.5 * normalized_kv_miss_delta + 0.3 * normalized_tpr_p99_delta + 0.2 * model_fallback_rate

Appendix B — Example incident Slack message (copy template)
---------------------------------------------------------
- Channel: #cs-early-warning
- Message: @oncall SRE, predictive-warning for tenant *$TENANT* (KV miss + TPR spike). Enrichment: <link to alert>. Action: running cache-prioritize; if latency 99p > 900ms in 15m escalate to Sev2.

Appendix C — Post-incident report template (fill-in)
---------------------------------------------------
- Incident ID:
- Tenant:
- Timeline: detection -> mitigation -> resolved (timestamps)
- Root cause:
- Mitigation steps taken: automated and manual
- Customer impact: number of failed requests, duration, affected routes
- Action items (owner + due date)

Contacts and escalation URLs
--------------------------

- Incident ticketing (internal): https://issues.redwood.ai/browse/OPS
- On-call roster: https://people.redwood.ai/oncall-roster
